eventMetadata.context_description: Trader consensus on Polymarket positions 24°C as the leading outcome at 39.5% implied probability for Paris-Le Bourget Airport's highest temperature on May 9, reflecting convergence in short-range forecasts from Météo-France AROME, ECMWF, and GFS models toward daytime highs of 23-25°C. This follows a sharp warm-up after cooler early-May conditions (e.g., 15°C highs around May 5), driven by advection of milder Mediterranean air masses under a temporary anticyclone ridge extending from the Baltic, with May 8 forecasts at 22°C amid post-storm clearing. Inherent spring variability persists, however, with potential afternoon showers or thunderstorms—signaled in latest outlooks—possibly capping peaks below 25°C; monitor final 00Z model runs and morning soundings for shifts. Above May climatology (~19°C average high), consistent with ongoing positive temperature anomalies.

eventMetadata.context_description: Latest INMET forecasts project a maximum temperature of 28°C for São Paulo on May 9 under mostly cloudy conditions with light northerly winds and low humidity, driving trader consensus toward 29°C (25.5% implied probability), 28°C (23.5%), and 27°C (21.0%) amid tight clustering. Southeast Brazil's persistent high-pressure ridge has sustained above-average early-May warmth (historical highs ~23–24°C), with dry stability over the past week limiting cooling. New INMET advisories and model updates expected by May 8 could sharpen resolution odds.

eventMetadata.context_description: Trader consensus on Polymarket assigns just 3.5% implied probability each to 8°C or below, 9°C, and 10°C highs in Helsinki on May 9, reflecting low confidence in prolonged cool conditions amid latest Finnish Meteorological Institute (FMI) forecasts showing daytime peaks near 11–13°C under northerly winds and partial clearing. Recent 24-hour model updates from ECMWF and GFS ensembles indicate a strengthening high-pressure ridge over Scandinavia, boosting diurnal heating and limiting cold air advection, which historically yields May 9 averages around 13°C at Helsinki-Vantaa station. Closely matched leading outcomes in the 11–14°C range stem from uncertainty in cloud cover persistence and boundary layer mixing, with overcast scenarios capping at lower teens versus sunnier runs pushing toward 14°C; new FMI briefings and 12Z model runs expected tomorrow could refine this spread before resolution via official FMI observations.

eventMetadata.context_description: Trader consensus on Polymarket reflects tight uncertainty in Beijing's May 10 highest temperature, with 32°C (22%), 33°C (21%), and 31°C (19.5%) leading amid forecasts from the China Meteorological Administration indicating a 31°C peak under cloudy skies and light southwest breezes. Differentiating factors include potential afternoon cloud thinning boosting insolation for 32–33°C versus sustained overcast capping at 31°C; GFS and ECMWF ensembles show 1–2°C spreads. Watch CMA updates and model refreshes by May 9 for shifts ahead of peak heating 2–4 p.m. local time.

May climatologically brings Manila's peak temperatures averaging 33–34°C, with minimal precipitation before the monsoon onset. Traders monitor daily PAGASA updates for refinements, as cloud cover or isolated showers could trim peaks, while sustained sunshine supports 35°C or higher at official stations.
